editorial: After the Shredder is gone, the four turtle brothers have drifted apart and lost their way as a family. Splinter worries about them while strange things start happening across New York City. You follow Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello, and Michelangelo as they try to pull back together and face a new threat. The movie has a fun, adventurous vibe with plenty of humor and heart. The animation looks great and gives the turtles a fresh, modern look while keeping their classic personalities. The story balances action with family drama, so it never feels boring. You get cool fight scenes, funny one-liners, and touching moments between brothers. Some parts move a little slow, and the villain plot can feel confusing at first. Still, the energy picks up fast and keeps you entertained. If you grew up with the turtles or want a fun family movie night, this one is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, the turtles discover that a wealthy businessman named Max Winters is actually an immortal warlord who wants to open a portal and release thirteen monsters to gain power. The turtles team up with their old friends April and Casey to stop him. Raphael and Leonardo finally settle their rivalry and fight side by side. In the end, the turtles defeat Winters and close the portal. The monsters are sent back, and the brothers reunite as a family, ready for whatever comes next.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated action and family-friendly adventure
